info.name: Restful-Booker API - chained flow and negative tests
info.description:
Stateful, self-cleaning test suite for https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com.

**Folder 01** chains Auth -> Create -> Update -> Verify -> Delete, passing the token and booking id between requests with collection variables.
**Folder 02** holds negative tests (missing/invalid token, invalid payloads, unknown ids) with its own setup and teardown.

Run: `npm test` (Newman) or import into Postman and use the Collection Runner. The public instance can cold-start slowly; use a generous request timeout.

item.name: POST /auth - wrong password issues no token

exec: const body = (function () { try { return pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { return undefined; } })();
pm.test('request is answered with 200 (documented) or 401 (REST-correct)', function () {

request.description:
Negative: valid username, wrong password.

Observed/documented behaviour: the API answers **200 OK** with `{"reason":"Bad credentials"}` instead of 401. The test asserts the security-relevant outcome (no token) and the documented reason, and tolerates 401 so it keeps passing if the API is corrected.

request.description: Negative: a username that does not exist. Same expectations as the wrong-password case.

item.name: POST /booking - missing required field (lastname) is rejected

exec: const body = (function () { try { return pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { return undefined; } })();
pm.test('request is rejected with a 4xx/5xx status (not 2xx)', function () {
pm.test('no booking was created (no bookingid in the response)', function () {

request.description: Negative: `lastname` is required. The API rejects the request; today it does so with **500 Internal Server Error** (400 would be the correct status for bad input), so the test accepts any 4xx/5xx and, more importantly, asserts that no booking was created.

item.name: PUT /booking/:id - without a token is forbidden

exec: var hostile = Object.assign({}, original, { firstname: 'Hacker', totalprice: 1 });
const body = (function () { try { return pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { return undefined; } })();
pm.test('PUT without a token returns 403 Forbidden', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(403); });
pm.test('no booking data is returned', function () {

request.description: Negative (required by the brief): attempts a valid update with **no** Cookie/Authorization header. Expected: 403 Forbidden and no booking data in the response.

item.name: GET /booking - malformed date filter is rejected

exec: const body = (function () { try { return pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { return undefined; } })();
pm.test('malformed date filter is not answered with 2xx', function () {

request.description: Negative: `checkin=not-a-date`. A well-behaved API returns 400. Today the unhandled date parse is expected to surface as a 5xx; the test requires that the API does **not** answer 2xx (silently ignoring the filter would return every booking).
